ctx: seeker: I know I'm not alone and that's what makes it hard to reach out, because I don't want people to think that I think my problems are worse then there's.  It just seems like everyone was happy to find different ways to stay in touch when the lockdown all first started but the longer it goes on the less everyone seems to be trying to connect.

supporter: That will give yourself too much emotion burden for sure.  Have you visited a physician for suggestion of your pain relief? Maybe yoga will be a more gentle way to replace dancing. What do you think?

actions.correct_action:
seeker: It is a lot, I'm used to being the person that everyone comes to for help, but I am not very good at asking for help myself.  I have seen a doctor and they started my new medicine regimen but unfortunately there is no cure for this disease.  I was going to physical therapy but finished that right as Covid started. Plus it does get better as the weather gets warmer so the winter has been hard, really looking forward to spring and summer for a little relief
supporter: I'm sorry to hear that no good medicine for your issue rite now. 
seeker: I'd be open to doing Yoga once things open back up, but having this disease puts me in a high risk category so my interaction outside the home still has to remain limited until we develop some heard immunity.
supporter: I know. Sunshine is always best cure for a better mood. Did you try to maybe walk or drive around your neighborhood for some fresh air?  Oh, then drive around might be the only option
Belief:
seeker: I've been feeling this way for a while, honestly. I've always been someone who prefers helping others over asking for help myself. My doctors have been supportive, and while there's no ultimate solution for my condition, they've helped manage some of the discomfort. I'm grateful for that guidance. The lack of social interaction during winter made it harder, but as it turns warmer, I'm hopeful for better days.
 supporter: It sounds like your doctors are doing their best. Even though the medicine isn't a cure, managing symptoms is a step towards feeling better. 
 seeker: I've considered new activities, like starting Yoga eventually, but I'm still cautious about stepping outside too much because of my health risks. The world is slowly opening, but it's still a tough decision to make.
 supporter: Understandably, safety comes first. Even small activities like indoor stretches or virtual classes might help. Connecting virtually with loved ones can also be uplifting.

seeker: Sometimes it feels like I'm carrying everything alone, even though I know others might want to help. I have been trying to manage with the new medication but it hasn't been easy. Winter always takes a toll, so I'm looking forward to the warmth of spring.
 supporter: I'm really sorry that the medication hasn't brought the relief you hoped for. 
 seeker: I'm considering trying yoga at home. I've read it can be beneficial, but I'm cautious about going out until things improve with the pandemic.
 supporter: That sounds like a great idea. Even indoor activities can be refreshing. Have you thought about trying some online classes to get started?

seeker: I've always been the one giving support, and it's hard to change that role now. I did speak to my doctor, and the medications help some, but it's more about management than a cure. Before everything shut down, I was attending a therapy group and I really miss that connection.
supporter: It's great that you had a group to rely on. Maybe there are online support groups you could join? 
seeker: That's a good idea, actually. I've been so cautious because of my health, and online groups might be a safer option for now. Once things settle, I'd like to try new activities safely.
supporter: Absolutely. Maybe online classes for now? It's amazing how technology can connect us until we're able to safely get back out there.
Desires:

 seeker: Yeah, I think being cautious is key right now. Once it feels safer, I would like to try joining an online community or group to stay connected.
 supporter: That sounds like a great idea! Virtual meet-ups are a wonderful way to connect without the risk. Let me know if you need help finding some groups online.

seeker: It's tough, I feel like I'm the one people turn to, but it's hard for me to reach out myself. I've been taking my medications, but the situation hasn't improved much. I finished physical therapy before the pandemic, and I'm hoping the warmer weather helps too.

 supporter: It makes sense to be careful. Indoor activities can be nice, too. Maybe meditation or virtual workouts could help you feel more connected.

seeker: I've always tried to be strong for others, but I guess now I'm seeing how much I need others, too. The doctor said to keep up with the exercises at home, and warmer days do make things more bearable, so I'm holding onto that hope.
 supporter: It's tough to be in that position, but reaching out can help. Maybe focusing on small joys that the warmer weather brings you could be uplifting, like a new book or hobby.
 seeker: I really like the idea of picking up something new. Sometimes, exploring different activities around the house is all I can do to stay engaged.
 supporter: That's a great way to keep positive. Have you thought about any online groups or classes where you could connect with others and try out those activities?
Intentions:
seeker: I might give yoga a try. It could help me manage things better. I've been thinking a lot about how I can cope.
 supporter: It's great that you're considering new options. Yoga can be really beneficial for stress and pain management.
 seeker: I want to explore more relaxing activities. This situation has really pushed me to find other ways to deal with everything.
 supporter: Absolutely, trying new things can bring positive changes. Meditation alongside yoga might also be helpful.

seeker: I'm going to try practicing yoga at home since I'm not comfortable going out yet. It's hard adjusting to this new routine, but hopefully it helps with the pain and stress.

 seeker: I haven't decided on a specific type yet, maybe something gentle to start with. I hope it can also help me become more mindful and relaxed.

seeker: That might be a good idea. I've thought about it but haven't tried it yet. I guess I'm still figuring out where to start, especially with so many options. 
supporter: Starting can be the hardest part. Maybe look for groups specifically for people who are navigating chronic conditions? It could feel reassuring to connect with others who understand your challenges.
